transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. 

Um... I guess I came in because I've been having a little bit of trouble with... well, sitting still, I guess. I mean, I really try to be professional and tough it out—I've been trying for months now—but whenever I'm supposed to just sit quietly in the radiology suite for my training, or in my classes, I just get this intense feeling like I'm crawling out of my skin. 

I really try not to be disruptive, I promise, but I always end up shifting around a lot, or pacing, or just having to find some excuse to get up and move. I hope it's okay that I came in for that... does that make sense?
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications—such as antipsychotics, anti-nausea drugs, or other prescriptions—around the time this restlessness began?

Oh, um, no. No, I haven't. I don't take any medications at all, actually. Definitely no antipsychotics or anti-nausea pills or... or any other prescriptions. 

I really try to stay healthy and take good care of myself, so I haven't started anything new or changed anything. Um, I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information... is it okay that I'm not on anything like that? I can write down the vitamins I take if you need me to, I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.

When you feel this need to move or pace, is it usually linked to worrying thoughts running through your mind, or does it feel more like a purely physical urge to move even when your mind isn't particularly anxious?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I'm really worrying about anything. I mean, I try to be a pretty positive person, you know? I definitely don't want you to think I'm, like, overly stressed out or anxious or anything bad like that. 

It's... it's really just this physical feeling. Like my body just kind of... won't settle down, I guess? Even when my mind is completely fine and I'm just trying to be a good student and pay attention to the instructor, I just get that physical urge to move my legs. 

Is that a normal thing to happen? I really hope I'm explaining this okay... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer.
Do you notice that this urge to move is worse in the evenings or when you're sitting still for a while, and does actually moving or stretching your legs make the sensation go away, even temporarily?

Oh, um... no, I haven't really noticed it being worse in the evenings. I mean, I really try to be quiet and just relax at night so I'm well-rested for my clinicals and don't bother my roommates. 

It definitely happens when I've been sitting still for a while, like I was saying before, but... stretching my legs doesn't really make the feeling go away. Like, getting up to pace feels better than just sitting there forcing myself to be still, but the urge to move doesn't actually stop. I just kind of always have this... this motor running, I guess? 

I hope that makes sense. I'm sorry if that's not the normal way it's supposed to happen, I just want to make sure I'm being completely honest with you. Is that a helpful answer? I can try to pay closer attention to it at night if you want me to!
Has this restless, need-to-move feeling been part of your life since childhood, or is this something that started only in the past few months?

Oh, um... well, no, it's definitely not just from the past few months. It's... it's been around since I was really little. I hope it's okay to admit this, but my parents actually still talk about my old elementary school conferences. The teachers would say I was always out of my seat, or calling out, or rushing ahead before they even finished giving the directions. 

I promise I wasn't trying to be disruptive or a bad kid or anything! I think I was just really eager to participate, you know? But yeah, that was happening way before middle school, not just since I started my radiology training. It's just always kind of been how I am. 

Is... is that the kind of timeline you needed to know? I really try my absolute best to be respectful of my instructors now, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right history.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a lifelong pattern (since elementary school) of motor restlessness, difficulty remaining seated, calling out, and acting before instructions are finished—classic hyperactive-impulsive symptoms. Current symptoms (pacing, inability to sit still in class/clinical settings) are a continuation of this childhood pattern rather than a new-onset phenomenon. Medication-induced akathisia was ruled out (no antipsychotic, antiemetic, or other precipitating drug exposure), and the urge to move is not preceded by anxious cognitions, arguing against generalized anxiety disorder. The lack of a circadian (evening-predominant) pattern and lack of relief with leg stretching make restless legs syndrome (G25.71) less likely. The chronic, early-onset, cross-situational hyperactive-impulsive presentation best fits ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation.
